titleStmt.title: Delayed Rate Monotonic with Semi-partitioned Technique Adapted to Multiprocessors

analytic.title: Delayed Rate Monotonic with Semi-partitioned Technique Adapted to Multiprocessors

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: This paper presents a semi-partitioned scheduling algorithm for periodic tasks on multiprocessor platforms. The scheduling policy used within each processor is based on delayed rate monotonic algorithm. Delayed rate monotonic is a modified version of rate monotonic algorithm, which can achieve higher processor utilization than rate monotonic. First, it is formally proved that any task which is feasible under rate monotonic is feasible under delayed rate monotonic, as well. Then, based on delayed rate monotonic, a new scheduling algorithm called adapted delayed rate monotonic (ADRM) is designed for multiprocessor systems. ADRM is composed of delayed rate monotonic algorithm and a semi-partitioned technique. Semi-partitioned is a new approach for allocating tasks on multiprocessor platforms. According to the simulation results, ADRM is safer against possible overload than rate monotonic algorithm. Then, a procedure is proposed to achieve processor utilization under ADRM algorithm more than the rate monotonic algorithm.

div.head: Keywords-real-time systems; delayed rate monotonic algorithm; semi-partitioned technique;
div.p: I.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Semi-partitioned technique is a new approach for allocating tasks on multiprocessor platforms. Nowadays, most computer systems are multiprocessors, hence, it is necessary for real-time systems to make use of multiprocessor platforms. Assigning a task to a processor is called allocation. It can be done in two, static or dynamic, manners. In dynamic allocation, only one queue exists for entire system and tasks can run on different processors. This allocation method has high overhead. On the other hand, in static allocation (or partitioning), each processor has a separate queue and each task may only run on one processor. The problem of static allocation is very similar to binpacking which is known to be NP-Hard [3]. In recent years, a new approach called semi-partitioned has been proposed. In this approach, most tasks are assigned to a single processor, while a few tasks are allowed to be split into several subtasks and assigned to a different processors to improve utilization.

Delayed rate monotonic is a modified version of rate monotonic algorithm, which can achieve higher processor utilization than rate monotonic [13,14]. In this algorithm a new state called delayed is added to the system. All tasks, except the lowest priority task enter this state as they are requested. Delayed rate monotonic can schedule any task set composed of two tasks with total utilization less than or equal to one on a single processor.
In this paper, we propose a new semi-partitioned scheduling algorithm for periodic tasks on multiprocessor platforms based on delayed rate monotonic. Our novel contributions are presented as follows:

• First, it is formally proved that any task which is feasible under rate monotonic will be feasible under delayed rate monotonic, as well. Then, adapted delayed rate monotonic algorithm (ADRM) is propose which adapts the allocation method proposed in paper [5] with delayed rate monotonic algorithm. The scheduling policy using in [5] is based on rate monotonic. The use of delayed rate monotonic algorithm makes ADRM perform better against possible overload than rate monotonic.

• A procedure is designed to change the allocation method of ADRM in order to improve the processor utilization. This procedure is a new admission control based on response time analysis. The new admission control makes ADRM achieve higher processor utilization than rate monotonic. The simulation results demonstrate that ADRM achieves significantly better processor utilization in comparison to previous work.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section II, prior works are discussed; in Section III, basic concepts are introduced. Sections IV and V relate to allocation method and adapted delayed rate monotonic. Finally, evaluation and conclusion are discussed in Sections VI and VII.

div.head: II. PRIOR WORKS
div.p: The first semi-partitioned technique was used with EDF algorithm for soft real-time systems [1]. Then some papers work on periodic tasks [5,6,8,15]. An approach called PDMS_HPTS has been proposed which selects and splits the highest priority task on each processor [8]. Scheduler of processors in this paper is based on deadline monotonic and utilization of this approach is 60%.

In some other researches, the lowest priority task is selected for splitting, i.e. the proposed approach in [6]. In the proposed approach of paper [6], tasks are sorted in ascending order of their periods and then allocation is done by a first-fit method. Scheduler of processors is based on rate monotonic and the Schedulability test being used in this paper is R-bound [9]. This Schedulability test is proposed by Lauzac, Melhem and Mosse in 2003 and they noted that their approach is a sufficient condition for checking feasibility of tasks but with a good approximation [9]. It should be noted that tasks in paper [6] are divided in two groups, light (tasks with utilization lower than 0.5) and heavy (tasks with utilization more than or equal to 0.5). In this paper, light tasks are partitioned as mentioned above. For heavy tasks, an approach like PDMS_HPTS is used. It means that the highest priority task is selected and split. The least upper bound to the processor utilization for heavy tasks is 72%.

An approach called SPA2 is proposed in paper [15] by which the processor utilization reaches L&L bound1 under rate monotonic policy. The allocation method used in this paper is worst-fit. This method selects a processor with the least total utilization of tasks which have been assigned to it. Paper [5] uses the same allocation method but admission control in this paper is based on response time analysis and hence utilization of processor can be improved over [15]. There are also some works with sporadic tasks and semipartitioned technique [2,4,7].

Tasks are hard real-time and missing a deadline is not allowed as oppose to soft real-time in which scares deadline misses is tolerable [16]. div.p: (2) A semi-partitioned scheduling includes two phases. In the first phase, tasks are assigned to the processors. If a task cannot entirely be accommodated to a processor, it is split into two subtasks. These tasks are called split-tasks. The other tasks which are entirely assigned to a processor are called non-split tasks. These tasks always run on a single processor.

The second phase of a semi-partitioned scheduling is the policy to determine how to schedule assigned tasks on each processor. The Scheduler used within each processor is based on delayed rate monotonic, which is the improved version of rate monotonic [12]. In rate monotonic algorithm every task with lower period has higher priority. Besides, this algorithm is pre-emptive. Therefore, the lowest priority task has the highest probability for overrun. In delayed rate monotonic all tasks have a secure delay except the task with the lowest priority. Therefore, for tasks in this scheduler, these two queues are defined:
• Ready: task with the lowest priority directly enters this queue and other tasks enter when their delays are over.
• Delay: all tasks except the lowest priority one enter this queue as they are requested.

A task in the ready queue has higher priority over all tasks in the delay queue. If no tasks exist in the ready queue, then a task is selected from delay queue to run next. If this task is later preempted it will stay in the ready queue. Tasks in both ready and delay queues are scheduled based on rate monotonic algorithm. Suppose tasks are sorted in ascending order of their periods. Formula (3) calculates delay of each task.

div.p: Parameter α is a constant, which is used to adjust the amount of delay which is imposed on tasks. It can be a value varying between [0, 1]. Delay of tasks are maximum if α is equal to one.

It should be mentioned that the concept of delay, which is used by delayed rate monotonic is different from zero laxity [10]. If T i,k is period of the k'th request of task τ i and C i,k (t) is the remaining execution time of task τ i in time t. Then, laxity of task τ i in time t is defined as T i,k -(t + C i,k (t)). When this laxity is equal to zero, it's called zero laxity. A task with zero delay (i.e., a task whose state has to change from delay to ready) is not necessarily a Zero-laxity task.

div.head: B. Assigning normal tasks
div.p: After pre-assignment phase it is time for remaining tasks. These tasks are called normal tasks. Based on the sorting method, the lowest priority task is in front of the queue. Now, choose a processor among normal processors with the worst-fit method. It means the processor with the least load factor is chosen for assigning the current task. If all tasks (including new task) in this processor can be feasible and all can meet their deadlines, we can add the entire task to this processor. As mentioned, such a task is called a non-split task. If an infeasible task exists, then the new task should be split. This task is called a split-task. The first part is added to this processor and the second part is put back in front of the queue. After adding the first part to a processor, no other task or subtask is assigned to this processor.

If no normal processor exists, then a pre-assign processor is chosen. In this case, the pre-assign processor which has a task with the highest period is chosen for assigning. This process continues. If the queue of tasks is empty, we can say that all tasks are successfully assigned to processors. Algorithm 1 shows the pseudo code of allocation method of RM-TS.

Considering Algorithm 1, each subtask of a split-task is the highest priority task on its own processor. Only for the last subtask of a split task, this may not hold. Now, under rate monotonic algorithm, the first subtask of a split-task will start its execution as soon as it is requested and will run to end without any interruption. Other subtasks of a split-task should wait until the prior subtasks are completed, before starting to execute. It means the delay of each subtask of a split-task is equal to the total worst case execution time of prior subtasks. This delay is calculated as shown in Formula (6).

In delayed rate monotonic algorithm all tasks, except the lowest priority one, enter the delay queue before moving to the ready queue. Each task stays for a different time interval in the delay queue. To prove the feasibility of tasks exactly the same as rate monotonic algorithm, the delay of tasks have been changed in this proposal. Therefore, for admission control of ADRM, the response time analysis can be used. As mentioned, tasks in RM-TS are divided into several groups. In a general classification, we have non-split tasks and splittasks.
• Non-split tasks: these tasks are each entirely assigned to one processor.
• Split-tasks: these tasks are split into several subtasks and each assigned to a different processor. As mentioned, all subtasks of a split-task, except the last one, are the highest priority task.
Both heavy tasks and light tasks belong to the same groups, i.e. a non-split task can be heavy or light.

It should be mentioned that in ADRM, based on delayed rate monotonic algorithm, a non-split task which is in the delay queue and it is the highest priority in this queue can run next if the ready queue is empty. Following lemma is stated to guaranty feasibility of split-tasks.
Lemma 3. Split-tasks which are partitioned by ADRM can be safely scheduled under delayed rate monotonic.

Proof. As mentioned, delay of split-tasks is calculated by Formula 6. This is the same as what was done in paper [5]. According to Formula 6, delay of the first subtask is equal to zero and directly enters the ready queue. Subtasks in ADRM are executed when their delays are completely finished and entered ready queue. This is done to synchronize subtasks of a split-task. In this work, the same behavior for a split-task as it is regarded in RM-TS, is considered. More details on feasibility of the split-tasks are presented in paper [5].□ In this work, to use the advantages of delayed rate monotonic algorithm, such as its resilience against possible overload, the allocation method of RM-TS is adapted to this algorithm.

div.head: A. Changing assigning method
div.p: To improve the processor utilization under ADRM algorithm, one procedure is expressed. It is a new admission control based on response time analysis. Algorithm 2 shows the allocation method of ADRM which uses this procedure.

In new admission control of ADRM, we express one state in which floor 3 of the Relation 4 is used for calculating the worst response time of the lowest priority task. As shown in Algorithm 1 (from Lines 23 to 27), if the current normal task, i.e. τ i , can't be assigned to processor P a , then this task will be split into two subtasks τ 1 i and τ 2 i . A binary search is done for finding maximum value of worst case execution time of τ 1 i . This binary search tests variable values for C 1 i and if all tasks in processor P a including τ 1 i are feasible, then task τ 1 i is assigned to the processor P a . As mentioned, the worst response time of a task under rate monotonic algorithm is calculated by Formula 4. Now, in allocation method of ADRM and in such situation, sometimes floor of this relation is used for calculating worst response time of the lowest priority task. By use of this new admission control, we can obtain larger value for C 1 i and hence the processor utilization is improved.

The second row in Table IV demonstrates the second group of generated task sets. This group is generated in order to evaluate ADRM against overload. The total utilization of each task set, U (Г), is assumed to be equal to L&L bound of the number of processors, M, so that they can be completely assigned to the processors. The allocation method of RM-TS is used for assigning tasks. For producing overload, a task is randomly selected and its execution time is a bit increased. Then, the executions of these task sets are simulated under both rate monotonic algorithm and ADRM algorithm. For first evaluation, a task is randomly selected and its execution time is increased so that its overload factor is increased by 0.1 or 0.2. At the end, the average of these tests is saved for every number of processors. Figure 3(a) shows the result of this test. As shown in Figure 3(a), the success ratio of two algorithms, when the number of processors are high, is become closer. This is happened because the number of processors which are not overloaded, is increased as well.

In the second evaluation, for each processor, a task is randomly selected and the overload factor is added to its worst case execution time. Figures 3(b) and 3(c) show the result of this test for eight and 64 processors. The success ratio of two algorithms converges together as overload factor increases, because the number of processors with utilization larger than one, is increasing as well.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, a new scheduling algorithm called ADRM is proposed by combining delayed rate monotonic algorithm with a semi-partitioned technique. ADRM can schedule any task set which is feasible under rate monotonic algorithm. ADRM can also be more resilient against possible overload compared with rate monotonic algorithm. Further, it achieves the same utilization. Then, a procedure is expressed to achieve higher processor utilization in some special cases under ADRM algorithm. In our future works, to improve the processor utilization, some other procedures will be presented to change the allocation method of ADRM. Improving our evaluations like using more task sets and processors are other purposes in our future works well.
